name: Loquacious Courtier Technique
description: The character's stories and idle chitchat become more entertaining; her turns of phrase wittier, her comments more topical. She adds two dice to her Socialize Ability for the scene for every mote she spends, but cannot add more dice than she has dots in Socialize.

name: Sweeten-the-Tap Method
description: Used near a quantity of alcohol, the drink noticeably improves in quality, strength, and taste, lifting the mood of the room and reducing by 1 the difficulty of all Socialize rolls for anyone present and imbibing for the rest of the evening. However, should anyone botch a Socialize roll during the scene, an overreaction is more likely (frayed tempers, ill-advised seductions) — a side effect with no fixed mechanic, left to the Storyteller.

name: Seizing-the-Tongue Technique
description: A quick-witted Dragon-Blood nimbly steps out of a verbal pit and reestablishes the conversation without giving offense: the player may immediately reroll any Socialize roll. She must accept the second roll even if worse, and cannot spend more Essence for further rerolls. If this Charm is part of a Combo, Essence must be spent to reactivate all the other Charms in that Combo when the reroll takes place; Charms with separate dice rolls are not themselves rerolled.

name: Warm-Faced Seduction Style
description: The Exalt coaxes the seductive aura of a flickering candle to coalesce around her face, briefly becoming far more attractive to a character she is attempting to seduce. She momentarily increases her Socialize dice pool by up to five dice, solely for seducing the Charm's target; it cannot increase her Socialize Trait to more than double its base value.

name: Wary Yellow Dog Attitude
description: When a social situation unexpectedly turns violent, the Dragon-Blood quickly focuses. During an unexpected combat (not a planned military battle or the end of a monster hunt) she may activate this Charm to add 3 to her Initiative roll. It can only be used during the first three turns of an unexpected combat.

name: Brother-Against-Brother Insinuation
description: Both the target and the individual she is to be set against must be present. The Exalt spends the motes and makes a simple comment to one about the other ('I hear he's got plans that don't include you'), weakening the bonds of friendship or love between them for the rest of the scene (the resulting conflict is up to the Storyteller). Neither party immediately remembers who started the disagreement, though onlookers may notice. When the scene ends cooler heads prevail and they recall their friendship, returning to their prior relationship unless something terrible happened; the original target may recall the Exalt's well-timed phrase with a successful Intelligence + Socialize roll (difficulty = the Exalt's Manipulation). Well-known in the Realm; users can be charged or disgraced. It does not work if either target has a higher Essence than the Exalt.

name: Friend-to-All-Nations Attitude
description: The Dragon-Blood is equally at home on the Blessed Isle, in the Scavenger Lands, or in the barbaric reaches of the Wyld. While active she suffers no penalties to her Socialize for being in a strange land, so long as she speaks the local tongue; if she does not, she may suffer a minor penalty at the Storyteller's discretion, as she instinctively knows all the mores and manners of the culture. It is somewhat less effective in melting-pot cultures such as Nexus, but people there are more tolerant of cultural differences, so the net effect is the same.

name: Smoothing-Over-the-Past Technique
description: Causes a target's mind to temporarily skip over a single past event involving the Exalt that would reflect poorly on the current discussion — an event that must have included the Exalt herself — just for the current scene. Multiple events require multiple uses (like any reflexive Charm). When the scene ends the target becomes aware of what happened and is likely unhappy about any bargains struck; future uses on the same individual first require smoothing over the memory of having been fooled before, which can quickly become impossibly expensive in Essence. It does not work on characters whose Essence is higher than the user's.
